body:
Crypto markets are holding their breath at $2.78T market cap today, up a modest 0.34% as traders parse mixed signals from both technical and fundamental fronts. The action feels subdued despite decent weekly gains across major assets, with Bitcoin dominance steady at 58.3% suggesting money isn't rotating aggressively between assets yet. Fear & Greed ticked up to 47 from yesterday's 38, moving out of fear territory but still well short of the euphoria levels that typically mark local tops. Volume at $56.4B is respectable but not screaming conviction in either direction.

Bitcoin closed at $80,835, up 0.53% on the day and holding the psychologically critical $80,000 level that's been the line in the sand for weeks now. The 3.17% weekly gain shows underlying strength, but the real test comes at $82,500 resistance where sellers have consistently emerged. Support sits cleanly at $78,000, and a break there would likely trigger stops down to $75,000. The $17.69B daily volume suggests institutions are still engaged, but we need to see a decisive break above $82,500 to confirm the next leg higher toward our $90,000 target.

Ethereum managed 0.55% gains to $2,329.52, but continues to underperform Bitcoin on longer timeframes with just 0.90% weekly returns. The ETH/BTC ratio remains concerning for altcoin bulls, suggesting risk-off positioning within crypto itself. Uniswap exploded 9.59% today and 24.67% this week, likely catching up to DeFi rotation themes, while Solana's 12.02% weekly performance keeps it in the leadership pack at $93.94. Chainlink's 15.01% weekly surge to $10.48 suggests oracle tokens are finding favor again, but Cardano's -1.32% daily slide shows the market is still picking winners and losers aggressively.

The macro backdrop is getting interesting with the Senate Clarity Act markup date announced, which crypto industry players are celebrating as progress on regulatory clarity. Meanwhile, emerging market users treating exchanges like banking apps according to Binance speaks to crypto's utility thesis gaining traction globally. Trump Media's $406M Q1 loss on bitcoin markdowns adds a political dimension that could matter heading into election season. The quantum computing concerns flagged in Project Eleven's report about Bitcoin's migration timeline adds a longer-term technical risk that sophisticated money is starting to price in.

Key catalysts ahead include that Senate markup which could provide regulatory tailwinds, while technically Bitcoin needs to reclaim $82,500 to confirm the next impulse higher. Watch for any rotation signals if ETH starts outperforming BTC, as that typically marks risk-on phases in crypto. The bigger risk remains macro repricing if rates expectations shift, but for now the path of least resistance looks sideways to slightly higher as long as $80,000 holds on Bitcoin. A break below would change everything and likely trigger the $75,000 retest we've been expecting.
